applies_why: No; the judge does not weigh a pressed chain against a live link, because it says the challenged curse limb was dropped.
quote: C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "witnesses pressed against a link": reading one, K-C still requires chain-against-chain weighing of C4 even after the curse limb was dropped; reading two, a dropped limb leaves no live link to press against, so K-C does not govern this text.
why: K-C governs chain-against-chain weighing when pressed witnesses oppose a live link, but here the judge states the targeted limb was dropped, so there is no live link for K-C to require weighing.
